title: Hot-route protection config schema draft (per-route limits + priority rules)
content:
Purpose
- Draft schema for “hot-route capacity protection” policy config.
- Used by policy engine + propagated to API gateway + router.
- Not final; capturing current implementation constraints and open questions.

Non-goals (for this schema doc)
- Full pricing/packaging modeling.
- Dedicated kernel-level scheduling / per-customer GPU partitioning.

Primary consumers
- Policy engine: validates, versions, diff/rollout, caches.
- API gateway: per-tenant/per-route/per-region rate limits + standardized 429 payload.
- Router: priority lanes admission + queue caps + backpressure-driven shedding.
- Observability: emits reason codes + policy ids (must be cardinality-safe).

Glossary / terms
- tenant: Redwood org/account id.
- tier: service tier used for priority decisions (enterprise vs self_serve). NOTE: Dedicated customers may still have enterprise tier but also separate capacity pool; needs clarity.
- route: logical API route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions) + model family + optional “intent” classification.
- region: control-plane region / serving region identifier.
- lane: router queue lane (enterprise lane vs default lane).

Design constraints / assumptions (current)
- Schema must support:
  - per-route limits (RPS + concurrent + tokens/sec caps) keyed by tenant+route(+region).
  - quota hooks (daily/monthly usage) as an enforcement signal; must define fail-open vs fail-closed on metering lag.
  - priority policy (enterprise lane reservation + bounded starvation controls).
  - reason codes surfaced to customer (via 429 payload + headers) + internal metrics.
- Config must be “safe to roll out”: validation, dry-run mode, staged rollout by region.
- Cardinality constraints: policy labels should not include raw tenant id in metrics by default; gateway can include hashed/opaque tenant labels only on sampled logs.

Schema shape (JSON-ish)
Top-level document
- apiVersion: string
- kind: string ("HotRouteProtectionPolicy")
- metadata:
  - name: string (stable name)
  - policy_id: string (immutable UUID-ish, generated on create)
  - owner_team: string ("eng-platform" etc)
  - created_by: string (human)
  - created_at: RFC3339 string
  - description: string
- spec:
  - scope:
    - regions: [string] (optional; empty => all)
    - tenants: [string] (optional allowlist; empty => all)
    - routes: [RouteSelector]
  - defaults: DefaultPolicy (applies when route selector matches but route block omits fields)
  - routes: [RoutePolicy] (route-specific overrides)
  - rollout: RolloutPolicy

NOTE: Actual persisted schema will be JSON; we keep YAML examples for readability.

RouteSelector (matching)
- path: string (exact match preferred; allow prefix match only if explicit)
- method: string ("POST" / "GET")
- model: string (optional; exact or family alias)
- model_family: string (optional; ex: "llama-3", "qwen2")
- deployment_mode: string ("hosted" | "dedicated" | "private") optional
- tags: [string] optional (future; e.g. "top_enterprise", "hot_route")

DefaultPolicy
- tier_rules: [TierRule]
- error_behavior: ErrorBehavior
- telemetry: TelemetryPolicy

RoutePolicy
- selector: RouteSelector
- enabled: bool
- tier_rules: [TierRule] (optional override)
- notes: string (freeform)

TierRule
- tier: string ("enterprise" | "self_serve" | "internal"; confirm enum)
- rate_limit: RateLimitPolicy (optional)
- quota: QuotaPolicy (optional)
- router_lane: LanePolicy (optional)
- backpressure: BackpressurePolicy (optional)

RateLimitPolicy
- algorithm: string ("token_bucket" default)
- key: string ("tenant+route+region" default; must be one of supported key templates)
- rps:
  - steady: number
  - burst: number
  - window_seconds: number (default 1)
- concurrent_requests:
  - max: number
- tokens_per_second:
  - max: number
  - scope: string ("estimated" | "metered") NOTE: gateway can only do estimates; router can do measured tokens.
- on_limit:
  - action: string ("reject_429" | "defer" (future))
  - retry_after_seconds: number (static default; can be overridden by reason)

QuotaPolicy
- enabled: bool
- windows: [QuotaWindow]
- metering_lag_seconds: number (allowed lag before enforcement changes behavior)
- on_metering_unavailable: string ("fail_open" | "fail_closed" | "degrade")

QuotaWindow
- name: string ("daily" | "monthly" | custom)
- limit_tokens: number OR limit_requests: number (prefer tokens)
- reset: string ("utc_midnight" | "month_start")

LanePolicy (router)
- lane: string ("enterprise" | "default")
- min_reserved_capacity_pct: number (0-100)
- max_queue_depth: number
- fairness:
  - mode: string ("bounded_starvation" | "weighted_fair")
  - max_starvation_seconds: number (if bounded_starvation)
  - weight: number (if weighted_fair)

BackpressurePolicy (router)
- signals: [BackpressureSignal]
- actions: [BackpressureAction]

BackpressureSignal
- name: string ("queue_depth" | "prefill_saturation" | "decode_saturation" | "gpu_util")
- sample_period_ms: number
- threshold:
  - warn: number
  - shed: number
- source: string ("runtime" | "router")

BackpressureAction
- when: string ("warn" | "shed")
- apply_to_tiers: [string]
- behavior: string ("reject_429" | "reject_503" | "fallback_model" | "drop_stream") NOTE: "fallback_model" must be coordinated with routing policy engine.

ErrorBehavior
- response_format_version: string ("throttle_v1")
- include_retry_after: bool
- include_request_id: bool
- default_reason_code: string ("rate_limited")

TelemetryPolicy
- emit_policy_id: bool (careful: policy_id cardinality ok; tenant_id not ok)
- emit_route_id: bool (route label must be low-card)
- emit_reason_code: bool
- sample_denied_requests: number (0-1)

RolloutPolicy
- mode: string ("dry_run" | "enforce")
- staged_by_region: bool
- canary:
  - enabled: bool
  - tenant_allowlist: [string]
  - percent: number
- kill_switch:
  - flag_name: string
  - default_state: string ("off" recommended)

Example 1: Minimal policy for a single hot route (hosted) with enterprise lane reservation

apiVersion: "ri.redwood.ai/v1"
kind: "HotRouteProtectionPolicy"
metadata:
  name: "hot-route-chat-completions"
  policy_id: "pol_2b7c2f4c"
  owner_team: "eng-platform"
  created_by: "Jordan Lee"
  created_at: "2025-01-16T21:10:00Z"
  description: "Initial protection for /v1/chat/completions on top enterprise tenants"
spec:
  scope:
    regions: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]
    tenants: []
    routes:
      - path: "/v1/chat/completions"
        method: "POST"
        deployment_mode: "hosted"
  defaults:
    tier_rules:
      - tier: "self_serve"
        rate_limit:
          algorithm: "token_bucket"
          key: "tenant+route+region"
          rps: { steady: 50, burst: 100, window_seconds: 1 }
          concurrent_requests: { max: 30 }
          on_limit: { action: "reject_429", retry_after_seconds: 2 }
        router_lane:
          lane: "default"
          max_queue_depth: 200
          fairness: { mode: "bounded_starvation", max_starvation_seconds: 2 }
      - tier: "enterprise"
        rate_limit:
          algorithm: "token_bucket"
          key: "tenant+route+region"
          rps: { steady: 500, burst: 800, window_seconds: 1 }
          concurrent_requests: { max: 200 }
          on_limit: { action: "reject_429", retry_after_seconds: 1 }
        router_lane:
          lane: "enterprise"
          min_reserved_capacity_pct: 30
          max_queue_depth: 500
          fairness: { mode: "bounded_starvation", max_starvation_seconds: 1 }
        backpressure:
          signals:
            - name: "queue_depth"
              sample_period_ms: 250
              threshold: { warn: 350, shed: 450 }
              source: "router"
          actions:
            - when: "shed"
              apply_to_tiers: ["self_serve"]
              behavior: "reject_429"
    error_behavior:
      response_format_version: "throttle_v1"
      include_retry_after: true
      include_request_id: true
      default_reason_code: "over_capacity"
    telemetry:
      emit_policy_id: true
      emit_route_id: true
      emit_reason_code: true
      sample_denied_requests: 0.01
  routes: []
  rollout:
    mode: "dry_run"
    staged_by_region: true
    canary: { enabled: true, tenant_allowlist: [], percent: 5 }
    kill_switch: { flag_name: "hot_route_protection_global", default_state: "off" }

Example 2: Route policy override for a specific model family (more aggressive TPS cap)

spec:
  routes:
    - selector:
        path: "/v1/chat/completions"
        method: "POST"
        model_family: "llama-3"
      enabled: true
      tier_rules:
        - tier: "self_serve"
          rate_limit:
            tokens_per_second:
              max: 25000
              scope: "estimated"
          notes: "Self-serve llama-3 spikes caused decode saturation in us-east-1 during retry storms"

Standardized 429 response payload (throttle_v1)
Goal: stable customer-facing semantics + consistent SDK parsing.

Headers
- HTTP 429
- Retry-After: <seconds>
- x-redwood-request-id: <uuid>
- x-redwood-throttle-reason: <reason_code>
- x-redwood-policy-id: <pol_...> (optional; check security stance)

Body (JSON)
{
  "error": {
    "type": "throttled",
    "reason_code": "rate_limited" | "quota_exceeded" | "over_capacity" | "lane_shed" | "config_unavailable",
    "message": "Request throttled. Reduce request rate and retry after the indicated delay.",
    "retry_after_seconds": 2,
    "request_id": "req_...",
    "policy": {
      "id": "pol_...",
      "name": "hot-route-chat-completions"
    }
  }
}
NOTE: For this Drive draft, body shape is illustrative. Implementation should follow ADR-0148 + ENG-4826.

Migration notes (from existing systems)
Current state (before this program)
- Gateway has coarse per-tenant rate limits and global circuit breakers.
- Router has limited admission control; overload collapses are possible during burst + retries.
- Quotas are enforced mostly via billing/usage gating; not consistently tied into realtime admission.

Target state
- Single policy config source of truth (policy engine) producing:
  - gateway enforcement config (rate limits, headers, error format)
  - router enforcement config (lane assignment, queue caps, backpressure rules)

Migration steps (proposed)
1) Introduce schema + validation in policy engine (PR-18444).
   - Strict validation: reject unknown fields.
   - Defaulting behavior centralized (so gateway/router don’t implement inconsistent defaults).
2) “Shadow mode” / dry_run (rollout.mode=dry_run).
   - Emit metrics as if enforced (would_throttle_count) without actual rejection.
3) Turn on enforcement for self_serve tiers first.
   - Keep enterprise rules permissive until lane reservation is stable.
4) Enable enterprise lane + reservation.
   - Gradual region rollout (staged_by_region).
5) Hook quota enforcement once metering lag is understood.
   - Start with fail_open and observability; flip to degrade/fail_closed only after confidence.

Compatibility / versioning
- apiVersion must be bumped when:
  - meaning of existing field changes
  - required fields change
  - error payload semantics change
- Proposed rules:
  - v1: additive changes ok
  - v2: breaking changes only
- Gateways/routers should accept at least N-1 versions during rollout window.

Open questions (please comment inline)
1) Tier taxonomy
- Do we need "enterprise_dedicated" vs "enterprise_hosted"? Or do we separate by deployment_mode and keep tiers consistent?
2) “Route id” definition
- Is route just path+method, or path+method+model? We need consistent low-cardinality labels.
3) Tokens/sec enforcement location
- Gateway can only estimate TPS (based on input length heuristics). Router/runtime can do measured; how do we reconcile?
4) Config fetch failure policy
- If gateway can’t fetch policy: fail_open vs fail_closed? SRE preference seems fail_open for availability but can amplify overload; need tier-aware behavior.
5) Retry-After semantics
- Static vs dynamic (queue-based) retry-after? If dynamic, ensure we don’t leak internal queue depth or cause sync retry behavior.
6) Quota lag
- What is acceptable metering delay? Should schema include “max lag” which flips behavior to “degrade”? (e.g., over_capacity shedding instead of quota-based rejects)
7) Model fallback
- If we add “fallback_model” as an action, do we expose that in response payload? How does that interact with enterprise expectations?

Notes to self (Jordan)
- Align reason codes list with ENG-4826. Keep list small.
- Push “policy_id” usage: ok for logs, maybe omit from customer payload until Security signs off.
- Work with Allison (obs standards) on metric label set; avoid tenant id labels.

Next steps
- Review with Amara (gateway) + Mina (routing) on which fields are actually needed in v1.
- Add a short JSONSchema draft in PR-18444 (or link it here) once stable.
- Convert these examples into test fixtures used in policy engine validation.

Changelog
- 2025-01-16: initial draft created (schema shape + minimal examples)
- 2025-01-28: added backpressure sections and reason code notes
- 2025-02-03: added rollout/kill-switch block + migration steps
